## (2) The exact false-match chain in untracked/log/t653.log

scan_terminal iterated the WHOLE worker text (not just the last 8 KiB its docstring claimed) and found 4 candidates: every 'hit your session limit' quote in the wall-canary document the brief told the lane to read. Within 400 bytes after the quote, the SAME quoted document's prose contains 'tokens: no reading … claude api error' — a FAILURE_EVIDENCE_RX pattern ('tokens: no reading') — so the quote read as a terminal death. The reset '<time>' did not parse (RESET_RX needs digits), so FALLBACK_COOLDOWN_SECONDS=6h armed. The log's mtime was fresh because the lane is alive → within ARM_FRESHNESS_SECONDS → armed. scan_terminal hardcoded family='claude'. Each dispatch re-derived from the moving mtime → the lockout extended itself.

## (4) The fix, one paragraph

window_policy.py now arms a cooldown ONLY from a terminal run record (T628 stamp provider_limit / provider_reset_epoch / provider_reset_text, or T629 killed_by=provider-limit) whose model maps to the family being cooled; the worker log is never read (scan_terminal, the log mtime dating, and the logdir task scan are deleted). A lane with no exit/end is live and arms nothing. An unparseable/absent reset arms a death-anchored fallback (default 30 min, env WEIZIGO_WINDOW_FALLBACK_SECONDS) — stable across re-derivation — and the existing watch() nudge opens the one-lane probe window to verify the provider. bin/dispatch and bin/subagent both enforce the cooldown with a reason-required recorded override (--override-window-cooldown=<reason> → untracked/fleet-window-overrides.jsonl, append-only; dry-run records nothing).

## (5) D040 (T612 amend, acked 2026-08-22T20:13:21Z) — the enforcement decision

T612's probe EMPIRICALLY confirmed the false cooldown: a claude-haiku lane (T676) launched at ~20:1xZ while dispatch refused the whole family until 02:06Z ran to completion, exit 0, verified pass (findings/T676-class-c-triage.json); T674/T675 claude lanes were running. T612 also found the guard existed ONLY in bin/dispatch: bin/subagent — which dispatch itself calls — had no cooldown check, so the guard was ADVISORY and the probe went around it via the underlying layer. DECISION: ENFORCE at the real launch chokepoint (bin/subagent — every lane launch, dispatch or hand goes through it; fleet-keeper fires bin/dispatch; bakeoff is the one documented exception, it launches tools/runner directly). Both prior bin/subagent holders (T494, T552) are done; the one-writer hold was declared on the kanban (holds=[tools/window_policy.py, bin/subagent]) and cleared after commit. The refusal texts in both dispatch and subagent now state the guard is enforced at subagent; the only way past it is the recorded override. Rationale recorded in the findings: a guard whose strength depends on which entry point the caller happens to know about is a guard in name only; 'a guard people route around teaches everyone to route around guards' (T612); and the T677 record-only arming removes the false-arm class that made enforcement risky.

## (6) Fallback argument (brief item 3, 'prefer probing over assuming')

Old: FALLBACK_COOLDOWN_SECONDS=6h, anchored to a live log's mtime, uncheckable, self-extending — 'conservative' only in the direction of expense. New: 30 min, anchored to the DEATH moment (death_epoch + fallback), then the one-lane probe verifies. Observed death→reset gap in the incident class: 13 min (12:47Z → 13:00Z); a 6h fallback would have idled the fleet ~6h past a reopen that came 13 minutes later. Worst case with the new bound: ≤ horizon + probe window past the real reopen, one cheap lane per cycle against a genuinely-closed window, and a fresh death re-arms automatically. The bound is CHECKED by the probe, not assumed.

## (8) Remaining surfaces, stated honestly

- tools/bakeoff.sh launches tools/runner directly (never bin/subagent): bakeoff lanes bypass the cooldown gate. Bakeoff is a deliberate, operator-launched experiment harness with its own isolation gates; documented as a known surface rather than silently left.
- The 2026-08-22 outage lanes (T615/616/617/621/622) have run records predating T629's vocabulary (no killed_by) — they arm nothing today. Deliberate per the brief: the record is the only evidence and those records carry no classification; they are also long past ARM_FRESHNESS_SECONDS.
- T659 (tools/runner) is the forward source of the T628 stamp (provider_limit / provider_reset_epoch / provider_reset_text at finalize); window_policy already reads killed_by (T629) and parses provider_reset_text, so the policy is live without the stamp.
- T628 never committed its work (no findings/T628-*.json; window_policy.py/regression/dispatch-gate/keeper wiring sat uncommitted). This commit carries both the preserved T628 mechanisms and the T677 correction; the record should not read as an argument against having the guard — its purpose (never start a doomed lane) was sound and was validated tonight when it refused a real cooldown; its evidence source was wrong and is corrected.
